title: Mixed Comprehension Checkpoint
description: Mix pronouns, possession, questions, noun phrases, action frames, and context so understanding has to transfer across lesson boundaries.

sourceReview.notes: All Hawaiian examples are taken from the modern Reference Grammar of the Hawaiian Language. The questions test relationships and context rather than isolated translation.

activities.instruction: Track subject, object, and group size.
activities.prompt: Ua ʻike ʻo ia iā mākou i ke kula.
options: He/she saw us, three or more, at school
He/she saw two listeners at school
activities.answer: He/she saw us, three or more, at school
activities.explanation: ʻo ia is the subject; iā mākou is the object, a first-person plural exclusive group.

activities.instruction: Track who is going with whom.
activities.prompt: E hele ʻo ia me kāua i ke kula.
options: The speaker and one other, not listener

activities.prompt: Aia ʻo Kimo ma koʻu hale.
activities.support: What does the full sentence tell you?
options: Kimo is at the speaker's house
The speaker is at Kimo's house
activities.answer: Kimo is at the speaker's house
activities.explanation: ma koʻu hale means at my house.

activities.instruction: Identify the missing information and time orientation.
activities.prompt: Āhea ʻoe e hele mai ai?
activities.support: What is the speaker asking for?
activities.explanation: āhea asks when in future-oriented context.

activities.prompt: Ināhea ʻoe i hele mai ai?
activities.explanation: ināhea asks when in past context.

activities.prompt: ʻAʻole anei ʻoe i ʻike mai iā mākou?
activities.support: What kind of message is this?
options: A negative yes/no question addressed to one listener
activities.answer: A negative yes/no question addressed to one listener
activities.explanation: anei marks a yes/no question; ʻaʻole makes it negative; ʻoe addresses one listener; iā mākou refers to us, three or more.

activities.instruction: Track possession across two noun phrases.
activities.prompt: Aia ʻo ia me kona makuahine a me kona makua kāne.
activities.explanation: kona is third-person singular o-class possessive in both relationships.

activities.instruction: Track number before translating the noun.
activities.support: What meaning is contributed by nā?
activities.explanation: nā marks definite plural noun phrases.

activities.instruction: Identify what kind of answer belongs.
activities.support: What would a good answer supply?

activities.prompt: Aia paha lākou ma loko o ka hale.
options: Uncertainty: they might be inside the house
activities.answer: Uncertainty: they might be inside the house
activities.explanation: paha marks uncertainty such as maybe/might in this sourced example.
